log.msg: THE LAB READS 0 AND 0. Headless at 400/1280/1920/3440, one press of the one button: today's row reports 129px of nav movement and 225-236px of width change at 1280/1920/3440; the stable row reports 0 and 0 at all four. The page's own readout and an independent measurement of the same click agree exactly at every width. No console errors. Three traps on the way: (1) a demo host wearing .page is display:none unless it also says `default` - the arrangement contract at the top of Page.css - and the whole row measured 0x0 while the readouts dutifully said 0px; (2) .page-column-prose is 0.9em and every core column width is an em, so the demo needed font-size:1rem or its columns would be 90% of a real page's; (3) a demo box wider than a rail plus two reading columns proves the opposite of the point - both columns cap at 40em and pressing does nothing - so the demo is capped at 66rem.

AT 400 NOTHING MOVES, and it is core doing it, not me. Under 32em of row Page.css pages the row one column at a time (flex: 1 0 100%, set directly at line 573 so no token can disturb it): the previous column slides out by exactly the viewport width, 400.0px, and its width and every nav link inside it read 0px of change - on all four pages, on every click. The crumb strip above the row holds 37.7px tall with its first link at the same pixel through four levels of depth on all four pages, so the one surviving navigation surface on a phone is also the one that never moves. The lab reads 0 and 0 on BOTH halves at 400 for the same reason.

THE PROPOSAL IS ONE DECLARATION: Page.css line 300, `flex: var(--page-column-flex, 1 1 0)` becomes `0 0 clamp(40em, 42cqi, 46em)` - the same number line 305 already caps the column at. small, hug, fill and full are untouched (they set the token themselves); the default word and `large` change, and `large` needs a cqi term it does not have today or two of them scroll a 1920 screen. The < 32em phone regime cannot be disturbed: it sets flex directly, later, at the same specificity. What it costs is the scroll, and two tunings trade that away - freeze at the FLOOR (already shipped as .paging-nav-fixed) or freeze at a third of the row (34cqi, the only one that both stays still and keeps a 3440 screen full). Which one core takes is the owner's call, written up in proposal.md and doc/decisions.md rather than decided here.

assign.outcome:
**The navigation jumps up to 242px. One CSS declaration makes it 0.** Open a column on this site and the columns already open get narrower to pay for it: measured on four real pages, the worst click moved an open column **242px** sideways, changed its width by **181px**, and dropped a nav link **170px** down the page — all at 1280, the width most readers have.

[**The lab**](/imagine/design/navigation/) is one screen: the same three-level tree twice, one button that presses both, two numbers under each. Today's row reads **129px nav moved / 225px widths changed**. The stable row reads **0px / 0px**, at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440. Both rows are built from core's own column classes, so the left one is not a drawing of today's behaviour — it is today's behaviour; the right one has one extra class.

![the lab at 1920](lab-1920.png)

**The rule.** A column that is already open never changes width when a column opens to its right; the new column takes what is left over, and when nothing is left the row scrolls sideways — the Finder way — instead of squeezing what is open. In `core/Page/Page.css` that is **line 300**: `flex: var(--page-column-flex, 1 1 0)` becomes `0 0 clamp(40em, 42cqi, 46em)`, the same number line 305 already caps the column at. `small`, `hug`, `fill` and `full` are untouched; the phone regime cannot be disturbed.

**At 400 nothing moves already.** Core pages the row one column at a time: the previous column slides out by exactly 400.0px and its width and nav links read 0px of change, on all four pages. The crumb strip holds 37.7px tall with its first link at the same pixel, four levels deep.

- [The lab](/imagine/design/navigation/) — two rows, one button, two numbers
- [The numbers](/imagine/design/navigation/numbers/) — four pages x four widths, before and after
- [The mechanisms catalogue](/imagine/design/navigation/mechanisms/) — what was on this page before, now one click down, unchanged
- [`proposal.md`](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/nav-stability/proposal.md) — the exact CSS, the core lines it replaces, what each of the six width words becomes
- [`measurements.json`](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/nav-stability/measurements.json) — every column, every click, raw

**Left for the owner, with the reason.** Which way the rule is tuned is a taste call, not a bug: freezing at the **ceiling** (shipped here) keeps a 40em reading column and pays with a scroll at the third column; freezing at the **floor** fits four columns at 1280 and makes reading columns 16em (already shipped as `.paging-nav-fixed`); freezing at **a third of the row** (`34cqi`) is the only one that both stays still and keeps a 3440 screen full, but it adds a number to core's vocabulary. The three are compared in [`doc/decisions.md`](/imagine/design/navigation/doc/decisions.md). Also left: the `dn-` prefix line for `styles/css-scopes.txt`, written out verbatim in that same file — that file was outside this task's fence.
